label: miso 68 mothballs
definition: miso-68 (KEEPER, promoted 2026-07-16 by owner) -- mothballed-but-operating re-carry (the Cottonwood lane): the miso-67 keeper recipe plus ONE single-delta override, carry_operating_mothballs=True — re-carry each OA (mothballed) unit the canonical 2025ER snapshot's OP filter drops for backcast solve year Y iff it is OP in the year-matched EIA-860 vintage_<Y> (the zero-DOF vintage-status availability oracle; a unit truly idle in Y is OA in vintage_<Y> too). Per-UNIT from the vintage rows: Cottonwood 55358's partial mothball (4 of 8 units OA, ~572.6/568.7 MW in vintage_2023/2024, CC_REGULAR MISO-South; CAMPD shows the OA CTs running 88-91% of 2023 hours) re-carries only its OA-but-operating units; 2025 has no committed vintage and carries nothing (accepted under-carry, charter owner default). MECHANISM-ONLY (main - same-box base, which reproduces the keeper's -9.79 exactly): CC_REGULAR-2023 -9.79 FAIL -> -8.28 FAIL (+1.51 TWh toward actual, tol ±8.00 — 0.28 TWh short of the band), CC_REGULAR-2024 -4.22 -> -2.98 PASS (margin widens), 2025 byte-identical. Zero C1 status flips (15/16, fail set unchanged, sole fail magnitude shrunk); displaced classes (COAL_PRB/CT_PEAKER/import/ST_GAS, worst -0.44 TWh) all stay PASS; C3b veto holds; C3a/C3c FAIL in both arms (the F4-blocked price-formation lane, untouched). LOO 2023-2025: zero fitted DOF, 2023 improves, 2024 independently improves, 2025 untouched — no held-out degradation. Promoted on rule 1/11 structure-first grounds (owner, 2026-07-16): the honest fleet carries the real units even though the class stays out of band. Design: docs/handoffs/miso-cc-vintage-undercarry-plan-2026-07.md.
market_story: One measured fleet-status layer on the miso-67 recipe, zero fitted parameters: EIA-860's contemporaneous annual vintages become the availability oracle for mothballed-but-operating capacity. The canonical 2025ER snapshot files Cottonwood (55358) as OA - mothballed - so the backcast fleet dropped its four affected units (~570 MW of MISO-South CC_REGULAR) even though CAMPD shows those units running 88-91% of 2023 hours. The new carry_operating_mothballs channel (backcast-only, gated, ISO-agnostic) re-carries each snapshot-dropped OA unit for solve year Y iff the year-matched EIA-860 vintage_<Y> files it OP - EIA's own status for that year, so a unit truly idle in Y (OA in its vintage too) never re-enters; 2025 has no committed vintage and carries nothing (accepted under-carry, charter owner default). The carried units dispatch from the LP's own economics - availability bounds, never pinned to CAMPD MWh (rules 1/11/13): Cottonwood runs ~4.0 TWh at ~40% CF. Mechanism-only vs the same-box base (which reproduces the miso-67 keeper's -9.79 exactly): CC_REGULAR-2023 -9.79 -> -8.28 (closes 1.51 of the 1.79 TWh needed, 0.28 short of the +/-8.00 band), CC_REGULAR-2024 -4.22 -> -2.98 (PASS margin widens), 2025 byte-identical; displaced mid-merit classes (COAL_PRB/CT_PEAKER/import/ST_GAS, worst -0.44 TWh) all stay PASS; zero C1 status flips (15/16, same sole fail). LOO 2023-2025 clean: zero fitted DOF, 2023 improves, 2024 independently improves, 2025 untouched. Promoted structure-first: miso-68 matches the miso-67 keeper's C1 count on a strictly more complete fleet, shrinks the sole C1 fail, improves 2024, and degrades nothing. The residual -8.28 is a dispatch/price-formation question (the plant is carried; the LP under-dispatches it vs near-continuous actual operation), pointing at the F4-blocked price lane, not more fleet work. C3a-2025/C3c stay the parked price-formation lane (F4-blocked on OASIS max-gen event access).
